A 58-year-old female patient comes to the office with a 2-week history of intermittent, dull low back pain
following a slip on a wet floor. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and her only medication is a
multivitamin. Vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination in the prone position, the
following findings are noted: * Normal muscle strength, tone, and reflexes * Mild tenderness over the
sacrotuberous ligament * Deep sacral sulcus on the right * Posterior inferior lateral angle (ILA) on the
left * Lumbosacral junction that does not spring freely on compression * L5 flexed, rotated right, and
sidebent right What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) right sacral torsion on a right
oblique axis (B) left sacral torsion on a left oblique axis (C) right sacral rotation around a right oblique
axis (D) right sacral rotation around a left oblique axis (E) unilateral sacral flexion on the left (F) left
sacral rotation around a left oblique axis (G) unilateral sacral extension on the right (H) anterior sacral
base dysfunction (I) bilateral sacral flexion (J) left sacral rotation around a right oblique axis
 A. unilateral sacral flexion on the left
B. right sacral rotation around a right oblique axis
C. anterior sacral base dysfunction
D. left sacral torsion on a left oblique axis
E. right sacral torsion on a right oblique axis

F. left sacral rotation around a left oblique axis
G. left sacral rotation around a right oblique axis
H. right sacral rotation around a left oblique axis
I. bilateral sacral flexion
J. unilateral sacral extension on the right
